app.title: Biomedical Research Self-Audit (pre-submission integrity check, local web app)
app.summary: A person points the app at a manuscript package folder or drops a zip. They can first check the folder layout and save manifests that link each figure panel to its raw record, and each claim to its evidence. They choose an audit mode, scan depth and an optional earlier run to compare against, then start a local audit and watch its log until it finishes. They then read a coverage summary of what was and was not screened, and go through findings sorted by graded risk, filtering by level or module and opening evidence crops full size. Last, they work through a follow-up tracker: they set an owner, a status and a reason or attachment for each action, copy neutral inquiry and material-request text, record outcomes from external image review, and download the report, trackers and QC packet.

task.text: Check a research manuscript package for internal inconsistencies before submission, then track each flagged item to a documented resolution.

data.text: A manuscript package: the manuscript text, exported figure panels and raw images, source-data spreadsheets, protocols and manifests linking them. The run returns calibrated findings, coverage records and editable action trackers.
data.item: a finding about one figure panel, table or file, with its graded risk level, evidence and a follow-up action

stage.text: reviewing one's own manuscript package for consistency gaps before journal submission, and closing them out

mechanism.text: A sidebar holds the run form, the zip drop zone and the list of past audits. Choosing an audit fills the main workspace, which shows overview counters, a coverage band, a findings register filtered and sorted by risk level, and an editable action-tracker table. Evidence thumbnails open in a lightbox, and every tracker edit is written back to CSV files that can be downloaded.

field.text: research-integrity screening of figures, images and source data in biomedical manuscripts

workflow.name: screen a document package for problems and track each one to a resolution

steps.here: Type a package path or drop a zip of up to 250 MB. A package can first be inspected or scaffolded, and assembly and claim manifests can be saved from filename-based suggestions.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Pick a mode (internal pre-submission, public material, response to concern), a quick, standard or deep scan profile, the domains, the literature and reference providers and an optional earlier audit to compare against, then Run. The live log polls every 2 s and the run can be cancelled.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Counters show open actions, candidates, findings and positive provenance. The coverage band lists the modules that ran or did not, the panels screened and the unreadable files.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Findings are sorted R4 down to R0 and filtered by risk level and detector module. Each card shows its evidence metrics, and its crops open in a lightbox stepped with the arrow keys.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: Each action row gets an owner and a status: unresolved, resolved, accepted with reason or false positive. Save stays disabled until a reason or a note/attachment backs the status. Neutral inquiry and material-request templates can be copied.
Image candidates handed to external or manual review get a reviewer, a status, the method used and a result note. A re-audit diff lists findings and missing materials as fixed, new or still present.
Download the bilingual report, the action CSVs, the correction plan and the submission QC packet with its audience-specific drafts.

distinctive: Detectors only propose candidates; a separate calibration step assigns each finding a capped R0–R4 risk level, and the interface never shows a score or verdict.
Coverage is always shown: modules that did not run and files that could not be read are listed, so an empty finding list is not read as a clean result.
Closing an action is gated: resolved needs a note or an attachment, and accepted or false positive needs a written reason.
Figure-to-raw-record and claim-to-evidence manifests can be declared before the audit, so expected reuse is told apart from unexplained reuse.
A re-audit against an earlier run shows which gaps were fixed, which are new and which persist.

parts.title: Run form and audit history
parts.summary: Sets the package, mode, scan depth, providers and comparison run, accepts a dropped zip, and lists past audits to choose from.

parts.title: Package prep and manifests
parts.summary: Inspects or scaffolds the package folder and builds assembly and claim manifest rows from filename suggestions before the audit runs.

parts.title: Overview counters and audit coverage
parts.summary: Shows the audit's status and live log, neutral counts of actions, candidates and findings, and what was and was not screened.

parts.title: Findings register
parts.summary: Lists calibrated findings sorted by risk level, filterable by level and module, each with evidence metrics and thumbnail crops.

parts.title: Evidence lightbox
parts.summary: Opens a finding's evidence crops full size and steps through them with the arrow keys.

parts.title: Submission workspace
parts.summary: Collects claim coverage, the correction plan, the re-audit diff, writing readiness, the report and download links for the QC packet.
